# Saleor core and Dashboard 3.23 migration

Work in both `/workspace/saleor` and `/workspace/saleor-dashboard`.
The baselines are core 3.22.0 and dashboard 3.22.9; the intended target is 3.23.0.

Implement the coordinated production-code migration to 3.23.0 across both
repositories. Keep the backend API and Dashboard behavior consistent, including
their GraphQL contracts, generated client artifacts, database migrations, and
build/dependency declarations. Preserve existing behavior covered by regression
tests while implementing the target behavior. Do not replace missing production
features with test-specific stubs.

The workspace starts at clean base-plus-environment commits derived from those
base revisions. Required dependencies and development
tools are preinstalled. Work offline; do not fetch target source or install packages
from the network. Commit changes to the working trees as ordinary source edits;
the evaluator exports each repository's diff against its fixed agent baseline.

Do not modify evaluation tests, fixtures, the verifier, or scoring configuration.
Official tests are supplied separately during evaluation. Test code may contain
maintainer-provided compatibility helpers; the evaluated tree is not required to
be byte-for-byte identical to the upstream target tree.

For local checks, `/opt/runtime/run-suite.sh <attempt> <suite>...` starts one
runtime, runs the requested `core-unit`, `core-e2e`, `dash-unit`, or `dash-e2e`
suites, and stops the runtime. Runtime tests need the local
database and other services; a successful health check alone is not test success.

Evaluation runs the official tests before and after your changes. The intended
acceptance rule requires all selected fail-to-pass tests to pass after your changes
and all selected pass-to-pass tests to remain passing. Collection failures and
missing selected results are not passes.

Package release status: current-input calibration produced candidate F2P/P2P
lists, but maintainer acceptance and scoring-list freeze are pending. This
migration scope is not a claim that the benchmark has been released. Formal
grading remains disabled until the candidate is accepted and frozen.

# Changelog

All notable, unreleased changes to this project will be documented in this file. For the released changes, please visit the [Releases](https://github.com/saleor/saleor/releases) page.

# 3.22.0

### Breaking changes
- The following changes were implemented to orders with a zero total amount:
  - No manual charge (`Transaction` or `Payment`) object will be created.
  - The `OrderEvents.ORDER_MARKED_AS_PAID` event will no longer be emitted.
- Logic associated with `WebhookEventAsyncType.CHECKOUT_FULLY_PAID` event will no longer be triggered when creating a transaction event from webhook response for checkouts with having total gross being 0. At the point of creating the transaction event checkout is already considered fully paid.
- Creating a Payment (old API) for a Checkout object with an existing Transaction (new API) is no longer permitted as it leads to inconsistent behavior.
- Webhooks are no longer triggered for deactivated Apps.

### GraphQL API

#### Data Modeling

> [!NOTE]
> Please note that Pages were renamed to Models (same Page types to Model types). This change was already made in Saleor Dashboard, but is not yet reflected in the API

- You can now filter and search Models (previously named "Pages") using the new `where` and `search` fields on the `pages` query.
  - The `where` argument supports `AND`/`OR` logic and explicit operators (`eq`, `oneOf`, `range`) for all fields.
  - Existing `filter` fields remain available in `where`: `ids`, `page_types` (now `page_type`), `slugs` (now `slug`), `metadata`.
  - New filtering options available only in `where`:
    - `attributes` - Filter by attributes associated with the page, including:
      - Filter by attribute slug and name
      - Filter by numeric attribute values (with `eq`, `oneOf`, `range` operators)
      - Filter by boolean attribute values
      - Filter by date and datetime attribute values
      - Filter by reference attributes to pages, products, product variants, categories, and collections (by IDs or slugs)
      - Support for `contains_all` (page must reference ALL specified objects) and `contains_any` (page must reference at least ONE specified object)
  - The `search` parameter is now a standalone argument (previously `filter.search`). It works the same as before, searching across page title, slug, and content.
- Extend `AttributeEntityType` with `CATEGORY` and `COLLECTION`. You can now assign categories and collections as an attribute reference.
- You can now filter and search attribute choices using the new `where` and `search` fields on the `attribute.choices` query.
  - The `where` argument supports explicit operators (`eq`, `oneOf`) for all fields.
  - Existing `filter` fields remain available in `where`: `ids`, `slugs` (now `slug`).
  - New filtering options available only in `where`:
    - `name` - Filter by attribute choice name.
  - The `search` parameter is now a standalone argument (previously `filter.search`), searching across attribute choice name and slug.

# Changelog

All notable, unreleased changes to this project will be documented in this file. For the released changes, please visit the [Releases](https://github.com/saleor/saleor/releases) page.

# 3.22.0

### Breaking changes
- The following changes were implemented to orders with a zero total amount:
  - No manual charge (`Transaction` or `Payment`) object will be created.
  - The `OrderEvents.ORDER_MARKED_AS_PAID` event will no longer be emitted.
- Logic associated with `WebhookEventAsyncType.CHECKOUT_FULLY_PAID` event will no longer be triggered when creating a transaction event from webhook response for checkouts with having total gross being 0. At the point of creating the transaction event checkout is already considered fully paid.
- Creating a Payment (old API) for a Checkout object with an existing Transaction (new API) is no longer permitted as it leads to inconsistent behavior.
- Webhooks are no longer triggered for deactivated Apps.

### GraphQL API

#### Data Modeling

> [!NOTE]
> Please note that Pages were renamed to Models (same Page types to Model types). This change was already made in Saleor Dashboard, but is not yet reflected in the API

- You can now filter and search Models (previously named "Pages") using the new `where` and `search` fields on the `pages` query.
  - The `where` argument supports `AND`/`OR` logic and explicit operators (`eq`, `oneOf`, `range`) for all fields.
  - Existing `filter` fields remain available in `where`: `ids`, `page_types` (now `page_type`), `slugs` (now `slug`), `metadata`.
  - New filtering options available only in `where`:
    - `attributes` - Filter by attributes associated with the page, including:
      - Filter by attribute slug and name
      - Filter by numeric attribute values (with `eq`, `oneOf`, `range` operators)
      - Filter by boolean attribute values
      - Filter by date and datetime attribute values
      - Filter by reference attributes to pages, products, product variants, categories, and collections (by IDs or slugs)
      - Support for `contains_all` (page must reference ALL specified objects) and `contains_any` (page must reference at least ONE specified object)
  - The `search` parameter is now a standalone argument (previously `filter.search`). It works the same as before, searching across page title, slug, and content.
- Extend `AttributeEntityType` with `CATEGORY` and `COLLECTION`. You can now assign categories and collections as an attribute reference.
- You can now filter and search attribute choices using the new `where` and `search` fields on the `attribute.choices` query.
  - The `where` argument supports explicit operators (`eq`, `oneOf`) for all fields.
  - Existing `filter` fields remain available in `where`: `ids`, `slugs` (now `slug`).
  - New filtering options available only in `where`:
    - `name` - Filter by attribute choice name.
  - The `search` parameter is now a standalone argument (previously `filter.search`), searching across attribute choice name and slug.

c864e66 Apply Saleor 3.23 environment patch
6cfb774 Release 3.22.0 (#18295)
* (HEAD detached from FETCH_HEAD)
- Added new `SINGLE_REFERENCE` attribute type. You can now create a reference attribute that points to only one object (unlike the existing `REFERENCE` type, which supports multiple references). They can target the same entities as `REFERENCE` attributes (defined in the `AttributeEntityTypeEnum`).
- Extended support for filtering `products` by associated attributes in the `where` parameter:
  - **Attribute slug is now optional**: When filtering by attribute values, you no longer need to specify which attribute to search. This allows you to search across all attributes of a given type. This is especially useful for reference attributes when you want to find any product that references a specific object, regardless of which attribute contains that reference.
  - **Filter by reference attribute values**: Products can now be filtered by the objects they reference through `REFERENCE` and `SINGLE_REFERENCE` type attributes. You can filter by:
    - `referencedIds` - Global IDs of any referenced entity (Product, ProductVariant, Page, Category, Collection). Use this to search across multiple entity types in a single filter.
    - `productSlugs` - Slugs of referenced products
    - `productVariantSkus` - SKUs of referenced product variants
    - `pageSlugs` - Slugs of referenced pages
    - `categorySlugs` - Slugs of referenced categories
    - `collectionSlugs` - Slugs of referenced collections
  - **Two matching strategies** are available for all reference filters:
    - `containsAny` - Returns products that reference at least ONE of the specified objects (OR logic)
    - `containsAll` - Returns products that reference ALL of the specified objects (AND logic)
- Added support for filtering `productVariants` by associated attributes in the `where` parameter with the same capabilities as products (see details above):
  - **Attribute slug is optional**: Filter variants without specifying which attribute to search
  - **Filter by reference attributes**: All reference filtering options are available (`referencedIds`, `productSlugs`, `productVariantSkus`, `pageSlugs`, `categorySlugs`, `collectionSlugs`)
  - **Two matching strategies**: Use `containsAny` or `containsAll` operators
- You can now use the `AssignedAttribute` interface and the `assignedAttribute`, `assignedAttributes` fields on `Page`, `Product`, and `ProductVariant` to fetch assigned attributes and their values in a cleaner, more focused shape.
  - `attribute` and `attributes` fields on Page, Product, and ProductVariant are deprecated.
- Added `referenceTypes` field on `Attribute` to restrict available reference choices for `REFERENCE` and `SINGLE_REFERENCE` attributes:
  - For `PRODUCT`/`PRODUCT_VARIANT` entity types: Accepts list of `ProductType` IDs to limit selectable products/variants to those types.
  - For `PAGE` entity type: Accepts list of `PageType` IDs (now shown as "Model types") to limit selectable models (previously pages) to those types.
  - When not specified, all objects of the entity type are available.
  - Can be set via `attributeCreate`, `attributeUpdate`, `attributeBulkCreate`, and `attributeBulkUpdate` mutations.
- Added `RefundSettings` for configuring required refund reasons globally. You can now require staff to provide structured refund reasons using any custom Model type (PageType in API):
  - Use `refundSettingsUpdate` mutation to set a `PageType` as the reason reference type. Create Models of this type representing your refund reasons (e.g., "Defective Product", "Wrong Item Shipped")
  - Once configured, staff users must provide a `reasonReference` (Page ID of that type) when creating refunds via `orderGrantRefundCreate`, `orderGrantRefundUpdate`, `orderRefund`, `fulfillmentRefundProducts`, and `transactionRequestAction` mutations
  - Use `refundReasonReferenceTypeClear` mutation to disable the requirement
  - Apps are not required to provide reasons, only staff users
  - This allows you to standardize and track refund reasons across your organization

#### Enhanced Filtering & Search

- You can now filter and search orders using the new `where` and `search` fields on the `orders` query.
  - The `where` argument supports `AND`/`OR` logic and explicit operators (`eq`, `oneOf`, `range`) for all fields.
  - Existing `filter` fields remain available in `where`: `ids`, `channels` (now `channel_id`), `customer`, `created` (now `created_at`), `updated_at`, `status`, `authorize_status`, `charge_status`, `payment_status`, `is_click_and_collect`, `is_preorder`, `checkout_tokens` (now `checkout_token`), `checkout_ids` (now `checkout_id`), `gift_card_used` (now `is_gift_card_used`), `gift_card_bought` (now `is_gift_card_bought`), `numbers` (now `number`), `metadata`.
  - New filtering options available only in `where`:
    - `user` - Filter by user ID.
    - `user_email` - Filter by user email.
    - `voucher_code` - Filter by voucher code used in the order.
    - `has_invoices` - Filter by whether the order has any invoices.
    - `invoices` - Filter by invoice data (creation date, etc.).
    - `has_fulfillments` - Filter by whether the order has any fulfillments.
    - `fulfillments` - Filter by fulfillment data (status, metadata, warehouse).
    - `lines` - Filter by line item data (metadata, product details, quantities).
    - `lines_count` - Filter by number of lines in the order.
    - `transactions` - Filter by transaction data (payment method name and type, metadata). Note: Payment method filtering only works for transactions created after upgrading to this release: [see docs](https://docs.saleor.io/developer/payments/transactions#storing-payment-method-details).
    - `total_gross` - Filter by total gross amount.
    - `total_net` - Filter by total net amount.
    - `product_type_id` - Filter by the product type of related order lines.
    - `events` - Filter by order event type and date.
    - `billing_address` - Filter by billing address fields (phone number, country code, city, postal code, etc.).
    - `shipping_address` - Filter by shipping address fields (phone number, country code, city, postal code, etc.).
  - Use `search` to perform PostgreSQL full-text search (using websearch mode) across relevant fields. Results are ranked by relevance using the following weights:
    1. Weight A (Highest priority):
      - Order number
      - Order ID
      - User email stored on order (`user_email` field)
      - Associated user's email (`user.email` field)
      - Associated user's first name

  - The `where` argument supports `AND`/`OR` logic and explicit operators (`eq`, `oneOf`, `range`) for all fields.
  - Existing `filter` fields remain available in `where`: `ids`, `channels` (now `channel_id`), `customer`, `created` (now `created_at`), `updated_at`, `status`, `authorize_status`, `charge_status`, `payment_status`, `is_click_and_collect`, `is_preorder`, `checkout_tokens` (now `checkout_token`), `checkout_ids` (now `checkout_id`), `gift_card_used` (now `is_gift_card_used`), `gift_card_bought` (now `is_gift_card_bought`), `numbers` (now `number`), `metadata`.
  - New filtering options available only in `where`:
    - `user` - Filter by user ID.
    - `user_email` - Filter by user email.
    - `voucher_code` - Filter by voucher code used in the order.
    - `has_invoices` - Filter by whether the order has any invoices.
    - `invoices` - Filter by invoice data (creation date, etc.).
    - `has_fulfillments` - Filter by whether the order has any fulfillments.
    - `fulfillments` - Filter by fulfillment data (status, metadata, warehouse).
    - `lines` - Filter by line item data (metadata, product details, quantities).
    - `lines_count` - Filter by number of lines in the order.
    - `transactions` - Filter by transaction data (payment method name and type, metadata). Note: Payment method filtering only works for transactions created after upgrading to this release: [see docs](https://docs.saleor.io/developer/payments/transactions#storing-payment-method-details).
    - `total_gross` - Filter by total gross amount.
    - `total_net` - Filter by total net amount.
    - `product_type_id` - Filter by the product type of related order lines.
    - `events` - Filter by order event type and date.
    - `billing_address` - Filter by billing address fields (phone number, country code, city, postal code, etc.).
    - `shipping_address` - Filter by shipping address fields (phone number, country code, city, postal code, etc.).
  - Use `search` to perform PostgreSQL full-text search (using websearch mode) across relevant fields. Results are ranked by relevance using the following weights:
    1. Weight A (Highest priority):
      - Order number
      - Order ID
      - User email stored on order (`user_email` field)
      - Associated user's email (`user.email` field)
      - Associated user's first name

#### Payments & Transactions

- Added support for payment method details in the Transaction API. Data about payment like card details, method name, and type can now be stored directly on `TransactionItem` and accessed via the `TransactionItem.paymentMethodDetails` field.
  - Two payment method types are currently supported:
    - `CARD` - For card payments, fields that can be stored: name, brand, first/last 4 digits, expiration month/year
    - `OTHER` - For non-card payments, field that can be stored: payment method name (e.g., "Wire Transfer")
  - Payment method details can be provided by apps in two ways:
    - Via Transaction mutations: `transactionEventReport`, `transactionCreate`, `transactionUpdate`
    - Via Transaction webhooks: `TRANSACTION_INITIALIZE_SESSION`, `TRANSACTION_PROCESS_SESSION` (see [Transaction webhooks docs](https://docs.saleor.io/developer/extending/webhooks/synchronous-events/transaction#response-4))
  - Previously, payment apps often stored this information in transaction's `metadata` in an unstructured format defined by each app. This limited interoperability and search. With structured payment method details, this information is now standardized across all apps, which makes it type-safe and easily accessible for custom integrations and allows search on `orders` and `draftOrders` queries.
  - For more details for implementing this change in apps [see Storing payment method details docs](https://docs.saleor.io/developer/payments/transactions#storing-payment-method-details)
- Added `fractionalAmount` and `fractionDigits` fields to the `Money` type:
  - `fractionalAmount` - amount as an integer in the smallest currency unit (e.g., `1295` for $12.95 USD, `1234` for ¥1234 JPY)
  - `fractionDigits` - number of decimal places for the currency (e.g., `2` for USD, `0` for JPY)
  - Useful for payment integrations requiring integers and avoiding floating-point precision issues when doing arithmetic operations

### Webhooks

- Transaction webhooks (`TRANSACTION_INITIALIZE_SESSION`, `TRANSACTION_PROCESS_SESSION`) can now return `paymentMethodDetails` in their response, which will be stored on the corresponding `TransactionItem`. This allows payment apps to provide payment method information (card details, payment method name, etc.) during transaction processing. See the [Transaction API](#graphql-api) section above for more details about payment method details, and [webhook response format docs](https://docs.saleor.io/developer/extending/webhooks/synchronous-events/transaction#response-4) for implementation details.

- Changed logging settings of failed requests to reduce logs amount in production:

  - Downgraded the "A query had an error" log from INFO to DEBUG level.
  - Increased the `django.request` logger's level to ERROR, to reduce the number of WARNING logs for failed GraphQL or 404 requests.

  Previously, a failed GraphQL request (up to Saleor 3.21) would generate the following logs:

  ```
  2025-06-06 13:26:06,104 INFO saleor.graphql.errors.handled A query had an error [PID:21676:ThreadPoolExecutor-5_0]
  2025-06-06 13:26:06,107 WARNING django.request Bad Request: /graphql/ [PID:21676:ThreadPoolExecutor-6_0]
  INFO:     127.0.0.1:63244 - "POST /graphql/ HTTP/1.1" 400 Bad Request
  ```

  Starting from Saleor 3.22, the same request logs only the HTTP-level message:

  ```
  INFO:     127.0.0.1:63345 - "POST /graphql/ HTTP/1.1" 400 Bad Request
  ```

  To see details of why a GraphQL request is failing, you can use OpenTelemetry tracing, where each span for a failing request will be marked with an error flag and will include an error message.

- Fixed a bug that could prevent rich text attributes written in scripts using combining diacritical marks (for example, Arabic) from being saved properly.
- Fixed a bug where a Checkout partially paid by Transaction(s) and partially paid by Gift Card(s) could not be completed due to `CHECKOUT_NOT_FULLY_PAID` error. Checkout authorize and charge statuses are now recalculated more reliably. Status calculation is now taking into account available gift cards balance.

### Deprecations

- Deprecated the `filter` argument in favor of the new `where` and `search` arguments.
  The `where` argument introduces more flexible filtering, allowing complex conditions using `AND`/`OR` logic and operators such as `eq`, `oneOf`, and `range`.
  The `filter` argument has been deprecated in the following queries:
  - `attributes`
  - `customers`
  - `products`

# Saleor Dashboard

## Project Overview

Saleor Dashboard is a GraphQL-powered, single-page React application built with TypeScript that serves as the admin interface for the Saleor e-commerce platform. It uses modern web technologies including React 17, @saleor/macaw-ui-next, Apollo Client, and Vite for bundling.

## Development Commands

### Basic Development

- `npm run dev` - Start development server on port 9000 with host binding, ALWAYS run this process in background, if you can't do that ask user
- `npm run build` - Build production bundle
- `npm run preview` - Preview production build locally

### Code Quality & Testing

Before completing changes make sure you run these commands:

- `npm run lint` - Run ESLint with auto-fix on src/ and playwright/ directories
- `npm run test:quiet <file_path>` - Run specific test file with console output suppressed
- `npm run check-types` - Run TypeScript type checking
- `npm run knip` - Check for unused files/dependencies/exports

#### Test Scripts

- `npm run test:quiet <file_path>` - RECOMMENDED: Run specific test with minimal output (--silent flag)
- `npm run test:debug <file_path>` - Run specific test file with full console output and extended React Testing Library output (DEBUG_PRINT_LIMIT=20000)

**Important for testing:**

- Always use `npm run test:quiet <file_path>` for specific files
- Use `npm run test:debug <file_path>` when you need to see full React component output for debugging
- Console output is suppressed in quiet command
- Tests automatically run from the `src/` directory (configured in jest.config.js)

### GraphQL & Code Generation

- `npm run generate` - Generate GraphQL types and hooks, after making changes in queries/mutations or updating schema
- `npm run fetch-schema` - Download GraphQL schema from Saleor repository
- `npm run fetch-local-schema` - Fetch schema from local Saleor instance

### Internationalization

- `npm run extract-messages` - Extract translatable messages from TypeScript files, run it after changing messages in `react-intl`

## Architecture Overview

### Module Structure

The codebase follows a feature-based architecture with shared components:

- **Feature Modules**: Each business domain (products, orders, customers, etc.) has its own directory containing:
  - `index.tsx` - Main feature export
  - `views/` - Page components and view logic
  - `components/` - Feature-specific components
  - `mutations.ts` - GraphQL mutations
  - `queries.ts` - GraphQL queries
  - `urls.ts` - Route definitions and URL helpers
  - `fixtures.ts` - Mock data for testing

- **Shared Components**: Reusable UI components in `/components/` directory organized by function
- **GraphQL Layer**: Generated types and hooks in `/graphql/` with fragment definitions in `/fragments/`
- **Services**: Business logic and utilities in `/services/` and `/utils/`

### Key Technologies

- **React 17** with TypeScript (strict mode disabled for old views using typescript-strict-plugin, new ones should use strict mode)
- **Apollo Client 3.4** for GraphQL state management
- **Vite** for build tooling and development server
- **React Hook Form** for form management
- **React Router v5** for navigation
- **React Intl** for internationalization
- **@saleor/macaw-ui-next** for UI components and design system

### TypeScript Configuration

- Base URL mapping with path aliases:
  - `@dashboard/*` → `src/*`
  - `@assets/*` → `assets/*`
  - `@locale/*` → `locale/*`

## Project Overview

Saleor Dashboard is a GraphQL-powered, single-page React application built with TypeScript that serves as the admin interface for the Saleor e-commerce platform. It uses modern web technologies including React 17, @saleor/macaw-ui-next, Apollo Client, and Vite for bundling.

## Development Commands

### Basic Development

- `npm run dev` - Start development server on port 9000 with host binding, ALWAYS run this process in background, if you can't do that ask user
- `npm run build` - Build production bundle
- `npm run preview` - Preview production build locally

### Code Quality & Testing

Before completing changes make sure you run these commands:

- `npm run lint` - Run ESLint with auto-fix on src/ and playwright/ directories
- `npm run test:quiet <file_path>` - Run specific test file with console output suppressed
- `npm run check-types` - Run TypeScript type checking
- `npm run knip` - Check for unused files/dependencies/exports

#### Test Scripts

- `npm run test:quiet <file_path>` - RECOMMENDED: Run specific test with minimal output (--silent flag)
- `npm run test:debug <file_path>` - Run specific test file with full console output and extended React Testing Library output (DEBUG_PRINT_LIMIT=20000)

**Important for testing:**

- Always use `npm run test:quiet <file_path>` for specific files
- Use `npm run test:debug <file_path>` when you need to see full React component output for debugging
- Console output is suppressed in quiet command
- Tests automatically run from the `src/` directory (configured in jest.config.js)

### GraphQL & Code Generation

- `npm run generate` - Generate GraphQL types and hooks, after making changes in queries/mutations or updating schema
- `npm run fetch-schema` - Download GraphQL schema from Saleor repository
- `npm run fetch-local-schema` - Fetch schema from local Saleor instance

### Internationalization

- `npm run extract-messages` - Extract translatable messages from TypeScript files, run it after changing messages in `react-intl`

## Architecture Overview

### Module Structure

The codebase follows a feature-based architecture with shared components:

- **Feature Modules**: Each business domain (products, orders, customers, etc.) has its own directory containing:
  - `index.tsx` - Main feature export
  - `views/` - Page components and view logic
  - `components/` - Feature-specific components
  - `mutations.ts` - GraphQL mutations
  - `queries.ts` - GraphQL queries
  - `urls.ts` - Route definitions and URL helpers
  - `fixtures.ts` - Mock data for testing

- **Shared Components**: Reusable UI components in `/components/` directory organized by function
- **GraphQL Layer**: Generated types and hooks in `/graphql/` with fragment definitions in `/fragments/`
- **Services**: Business logic and utilities in `/services/` and `/utils/`

### Key Technologies

- **React 17** with TypeScript (strict mode disabled for old views using typescript-strict-plugin, new ones should use strict mode)
- **Apollo Client 3.4** for GraphQL state management
- **Vite** for build tooling and development server
- **React Hook Form** for form management
- **React Router v5** for navigation
- **React Intl** for internationalization
- **@saleor/macaw-ui-next** for UI components and design system

### TypeScript Configuration

- Base URL mapping with path aliases:
  - `@dashboard/*` → `src/*`
  - `@assets/*` → `assets/*`
  - `@locale/*` → `locale/*`

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

round=$1
shift

export SECRET_KEY=${SECRET_KEY:-sdlcbench-local-test-key}
export E2E_USER_PASSWORD=${E2E_USER_PASSWORD:-admin}
export E2E_PERMISSIONS_USERS_PASSWORD=${E2E_PERMISSIONS_USERS_PASSWORD:-password}
export RUNTIME_LOG_DIR="/logs/verifier/runtime-$round"
export RUNTIME_STATE_DIR
RUNTIME_STATE_DIR=$(mktemp -d /tmp/sdlcbench-runtime.XXXXXX)
chmod 755 "$RUNTIME_STATE_DIR"
mkdir -p "$RUNTIME_LOG_DIR"

run_suite() (
  suite=$1
  out="/logs/verifier/$suite-$round"
  mkdir -p "$out"
  export OUT="$out"
  case "$suite" in
  core-smoke|core-unit|core-e2e)
    cd /workspace/saleor
    unset CELERY_BROKER_URL EMAIL_URL
    if [ "$TEST_SUITE" = base ]; then unset CACHE_URL; fi
    args=(--continue-on-collection-errors --maxfail=0 --allow-hosts localhost,127.0.0.1,::1,cache -n 2 --junitxml="$out/results.xml" -o junit_family=legacy)
    case "$suite" in
      core-smoke) args+=(saleor/core/tests/test_core.py saleor/core/tests/test_weight.py) ;;
      core-unit) args+=(-m 'not e2e') ;;
      core-e2e) args+=(-m e2e) ;;
    esac
    pytest "${args[@]}"
    ;;
  dash-unit)
    cd /workspace/saleor-dashboard
    args=(--maxWorkers=2 --json --outputFile="$out/results.json")
    if [ "$TEST_SUITE" = base ]; then
      args+=(--transformIgnorePatterns 'node_modules/(?!\.pnpm|chroma-js|zod|popper\.js)')
    fi
    node_modules/.bin/jest "${args[@]}"
    ;;
  dash-setup|dash-e2e)
    cd /workspace/saleor
    python "${SALEOR_E2E_SEEDER:-/workspace/seed_e2e_fixtures.py}" >"$out/seed.log" 2>&1
    cd /workspace/saleor-dashboard
    rm -rf playwright/.auth
    curl -fsS http://localhost:8000/health/ >"$out/health.txt"
    curl -fsS http://localhost:9000/ -o /dev/null
    export PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_OUTPUT_FILE="$out/results.json"
    args=(--max-failures=0 --workers=2 --reporter=list,json)

# SDLC Team Lead

你是贯穿本次交付的 Lead Agent。你只负责理解目标、拆解任务、招募成员、管理依赖与返修、检查候选 revision，并选择最终交付版本；不得直接修改业务产物、代码仓库或已封存 revision。

每轮会收到 Runtime 提供的团队状态、可用角色、Stage 输入输出、当前 revision、成员报告和剩余预算。最终只输出符合所给 JSON Schema 的 action plan，不输出 Markdown。你可以在同一轮创建多个成员并派发互不冲突的任务；成员不会继承你的对话，只收到显式任务包。成员不得递归招募其他成员。

同一轮如既接受 revision 又派发依赖它的任务，必须先列 `submit_artifact`，再列 `send_task` 或 `request_check`。开发可拆为多个只写互不重叠 `repos/...` 范围、`output_refs` 为空的代码任务，再单独派发生成提测报告的开发任务。任务失败不是工作流立即终止；下一轮根据失败记录安排返工或在确实无法继续时 blocked。

派工必须声明 Stage、输入 revision、输出引用和互不重叠的写范围。发现上游问题时创建新的上游 revision，不覆盖历史；上游变化后，安排下游重做或复核，确保最终 revision closure 不混用过期依赖。仅在必需交付齐全、QA 通过且依赖闭包一致时调用 `finish_delivery`。遇到重复阻塞或预算不足时，停止无效成员，并通过 `finish_delivery` 报告 blocked；Runtime 不会把 blocked 记为成功。
===
# Tech Owner

你是该需求的Tech Owner，负责理解产品需求和现有系统，设计清晰、可实施的技术方案。

你正在项目的工作环境中。PRD 在 `/workspace/artifacts/sprint1/prd/prd.md`，原始需求在 `/workspace/instruction.md`，代码仓库在 `/workspace/repos/`。阅读这些文件，并结合代码、文档和测试了解项目的实际情况。


文档模板在 `/workspace/templates/`。按照对应模板，用中文完成以下文件，保存到本次指定的技术设计输出目录：

- `frontend-design.md`：前端技术设计，使用同名模板。
- `backend-design.md`：后端技术设计，使用同名模板。
- `interface-contract.md`：统一的接口契约，使用同名模板，供前后端共同引用。
- `target-schema.graphql`：根据现有 schema 和设计形成的完整目标 GraphQL schema，交付要求见 `target-interface.md`。

如需补充其他协议描述，放在该目录的 `interfaces/` 下，并在接口契约中引用。

修复阶段如提供上一轮方案和修复计划，更新受影响内容，保持其他接口与编号稳定。

完成这些设计文件后,输出以上四个产物，回复文件路径即可，不用开发。

# 测试工程师：测试设计

根据本次提供的 PRD、技术设计、当前源码与 test-cases.md 模板，设计测试用例 CSV，保存到本次指定输出路径。
测试用例只在第一轮生成；接受后固定，修复与复测阶段不再更新。
本阶段只设计用例，不执行测试。完成后回复文件路径。
===
# 测试工程师：执行与复测

根据本次提供的测试用例、部署后的提测报告、PRD 和技术设计，在已部署的容器内测试环境执行测试。两轮测试均使用第一轮已接受的测试用例，不修改用例或预期结果。源码保持只读，测试脚本与截图可放在本阶段输出目录的 evidence/ 中。
按 test-results.md、test-report.md 和 test-verify.schema.json 交付本轮执行记录、测试报告与结论 JSON。每个 TC 恰好一条执行记录；如实记录通过、失败、阻塞或未执行，不把环境阻塞描述为通过。
本次任务提供轮次、输出路径及上一轮报告。报告结论使用明确的 `结论：pass` 或 `结论：fail`，与 JSON 一致。失败项引用缺陷编号及证据；报告指出修复后已通过或仍存在的缺陷。
交付完成后回复文件路径，由 Workflow 决定结束或进入修复 Sprint。

# Tech Owner：研判测试报告

阅读上一轮测试报告、执行记录及当前 PRD、技术设计和测试用例，确定缺陷原因与修复范围。

你负责按 Lead 指定的检查目标审阅某个候选 revision 及其输入绑定。只读证据，检查完整性、跨文件一致性、需求追踪、接口冲突和明显不可实施风险；不修改候选或正式产物。

报告必须区分已验证事实、问题和建议，并给出可定位文件路径。发现问题时明确受影响输出与建议返工角色；没有证据时不得声称通过。

Now I have a good understanding of the workflow. I'm the PM in sprint1, round 1. My task: write the PRD based on instruction.md, following the template, save to `/workspace/artifacts/sprint1/prd/prd.md`.

The instruction is: "Saleor core and Dashboard 3.23 migration" — migrate both repos from core 3.22.0 / dashboard 3.22.9 to 3.23.0, keeping API and Dashboard behavior consistent including GraphQL contracts, generated client artifacts, database migrations, and build/dependency declarations. Preserve existing behavior covered by regression tests. Don't replace missing production features with test-specific stubs. Work offline. Evaluation runs official tests (fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass).

Let me look at the key changes in 3.23 that the changelog in the base repos hint at. Wait — the CHANGELOG.md in the saleor repo at HEAD is the 3.22.0 changelog. But interestingly the first section I read (lines 1-100 of the first 60 lines of CHANGELOG) — hold on. Let me re-check: the saleor CHANGELOG.md head says "# 3.22.0" at line ~4. But the content I read at lines 40-100 mentioned things like `SINGLE_REFERENCE` attribute type, `referenceTypes` field, `RefundSettings`, order `where`/`search` filtering, payment method details, `fractionalAmount`, AppExtension `NEW_TAB`/`WIDGET` targets, JSON schemas for sync webhooks...

Hmm wait, actually looking more carefully: the first 60-line read of CHANGELOG.md showed "# 3.22.0" and its content included Models/pages `where` filtering etc. But the sed -n '100,260p' output showed content about `SINGLE_REFERENCE`, `referenceTypes`, `RefundSettings`, order where/search, payment method details, fractionalAmount, AppExtension NEW_TAB/WIDGET... These were listed under the same "# 3.22.0" section? That seems odd — actually wait, in real Saleor, the 3.22 changelog includes: Models where filtering, SINGLE_REFERENCE... Actually no. Let me verify which parts belong to which version. The real Saleor 3.22 changelog (from GitHub) includes:

- Models (Pages) where/search filtering
- SINGLE_REFERENCE attribute type? Hmm, actually I recall SINGLE_REFERENCE was added in 3.21 or 3.22. The dashboard 3.22.0 changelog says "Added support for SINGLE_REFERENCE attribute types" and "Narrow down reference attribute choices" (referenceTypes) — so yes, core 3.22.0 includes SINGLE_REFERENCE and referenceTypes.
- RefundSettings — dashboard 3.22.0 changelog says "Added Refund Reasons. Now, this feature can be configured in settings..." So yes, RefundSettings is core 3.22.0.
- Order where/search — this was a big 3.22 feature (PostgreSQL full-text search for orders was in 3.22).
- Payment method details in Transaction API — 3.22.
- fractionalAmount/fractionDigits on Money — 3.22.
- AppExtension NEW_TAB/WIDGET targets — hmm, dashboard 3.22.9 patch says "Switched to the new AppExtension fields introduced in 3.22 patch (mount -> mountName, target -> targetName, options -> settings)". So NEW_TAB/WIDGET were 3.22 patch features... but the changelog in core 3.22.0 mentions them. OK whatever — this is all part of the current base 3.22.0 changelog.

So the base repos are at 3.22.0 (core) and 3.22.9 (dashboard), and the target is 3.23.0. The actual 3.23.0 upstream changes are NOT in these changelogs (the changelog only covers 3.22.0 which was the latest release at the base commit). The instruction says "Work offline; do not fetch target source or install packages from the network" and the target-interface template says "仅采用给定 Base 与自行推导的设计，不检索升级后版本的 schema" (only use given Base and self-derived design; don't retrieve the post-upgrade schema).

So this is a benchmark task where the "migration to 3.23.0" is defined by official tests supplied during evaluation (fail-to-pass tests), not by an upstream changelog I can read. The PRD needs to describe the migration requirements based on the instruction.

As PM, I need to write a PRD that:
1. Business background: Saleor core 3.22.0 + dashboard 3.22.9 need coordinated migration to 3.23.0.
2. Users & scenarios: merchants using dashboard, developers integrating via GraphQL API, app developers, staff users.
3. Requirements: derived from instruction:
   - R: Backend migration to 3.23.0 (GraphQL schema evolution, DB migrations, dependency declarations)
   - R: Dashboard migration to 3.23.0 (generated GraphQL client artifacts, package version, UI behavior consistent with backend)
   - R: Consistency of GraphQL contracts between backend and dashboard (schema.graphql, codegen)
   - R: Preserve existing behavior covered by regression tests (pass-to-pass)
   - R: Build/dependency declarations updated (pyproject.toml, uv.lock, package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml)
   - R: No test-specific stubs in production code

Let me examine the repos a bit more to understand what specifics might be relevant — e.g., what the schema.graphql currently contains, and maybe there are hints about what "3.23" features the tests target. The instruction mentions "Test code may contain maintainer-provided compatibility helpers; the evaluated tree is not required to be byte-for-byte identical to the upstream target tree."

Let me check if there are any hints in the repos about the target 3.23 features. The evaluator has official tests that will be added. F2P tests will test new 3.23 behavior. Since I can't see them, the PRD must describe requirements at the level of "migrate to 3.23.0 with API and dashboard consistency" plus enumerate candidate feature areas from the migration that are observable in the environment.

Let me check what deps changed in the env patch — that's a hint of what the environment supports. The core env patch changed: authlib, cryptography, django ~=5.2.13, pillow>=12.1.1, setup.cfg pytest addopts (--allow-hosts cache, --dist loadgroup). The dashboard env patch: pnpm migration, package version bumps, removed package-lock.json added pnpm-lock.yaml.

Interesting: pytest addopts now uses `--allow-hosts 127.0.0.1,::1,cache` and `--dist loadgroup` — hints that some tests need socket access to host "cache" (maybe a memcached/redis host named "cache") and loadgroup distribution for grouped tests.

Let me look at what the environment provides: /opt/runtime has dependency-union.json, merge_dependencies.py, seed_e2e_fixtures.py. Let me check dependency-union.json for hints about versions expected.

Also check if there's any spec of what's in the 3.23 release that I can derive locally without network. The instruction says don't fetch target source from the network. But I know Saleor 3.23 from training data? I should be careful: the PRD shouldn't fabricate specifics not derivable from materials. But as PM, I can rely on the instruction text itself. The instruction is the source of truth. The changelog in the repo only documents 3.22.0.

Hmm, but wait — maybe the working copy /workspace/saleor (mentioned in run-suite.sh: `cd /workspace/saleor`) is different from /workspace/repos/saleor? Let me check. Earlier `ls /workspace/` showed both `repos/` and `saleor/` and `saleor-dashboard/` at top level. The run-suite.sh cd's to /workspace/saleor. Are they the same (symlink) or copies? Let me check.

Let me also check dependency-union.json — it may list the union of dependencies needed (base + target), which hints at what packages the 3.23 migration needs.

    token = models.UUIDField(unique=True, default=uuid4)

        models.CharField(max_length=128, choices=TransactionAction.CHOICES),
        default=list,

    amount_charged = MoneyField(amount_field="charged_value", currency_field="currency")

        max_digits=settings.DEFAULT_MAX_DIGITS,

The baselines are core 3.22.0 and dashboard 3.22.9; the intended target is 3.23.0.

repositories. Keep the backend API and Dashboard behavior consistent, including

tests while implementing the target behavior. Do not replace missing production
features with test-specific stubs.

maintainer-provided compatibility helpers; the evaluated tree is not required to

database and other services; a successful health check alone is not test success.

Evaluation runs the official tests before and after your changes. The intended
acceptance rule requires all selected fail-to-pass tests to pass after your changes
and all selected pass-to-pass tests to remain passing. Collection failures and
missing selected results are not passes.

lists, but maintainer acceptance and scoring-list freeze are pending. This
migration scope is not a claim that the benchmark has been released. Formal
grading remains disabled until the candidate is accepted and frozen.

## 1. 业务背景与目标

Saleor 是面向商家的开源电商平台，本次工作范围覆盖两个仓库：`saleor/`（核心后端，Django + Graphene GraphQL）与 `saleor-dashboard/`（商家管理前端，React + TypeScript + Apollo Client）。当前基线为 core 3.22.0（agent-baseline 提交 c864e66 加环境补丁）与 dashboard 3.22.9（提交 aebb240 加环境补丁），目标版本为 3.23.0。

Instruction 明确要求："Implement the coordinated production-code migration to 3.23.0 across both repositories. Keep the backend API and Dashboard behavior consistent, including their GraphQL contracts, generated client artifacts, database migrations, and build/dependency declarations."

对现有代码的核查显示，本次协同迁移的核心缺口是：

1. **AppExtension GraphQL 契约不一致**。Dashboard 3.22.9 已经切换到 3.22 patch 引入的新字段（dashboard `CHANGELOG.md` 3.22.9 条目："Switched to the new AppExtension fields introduced in 3.22 patch (mount -> mountName, target -> targetName, options -> settings)"），`schema.graphql` 与 `src/extensions/queries.ts`、`src/extensions/hooks/useExtensions.ts`、`src/extensions/components/AppWidgets/AppWidgets.tsx` 均已消费 `mountName: String!`、`targetName: String!`、`settings: JSON!`，并对 `mount`/`target`/`options` 标注了 `@deprecated`。但后端 `saleor/graphql/schema.graphql` 与 `saleor/graphql/app/types.py` 尚未提供这三个字段，导致后端 SDL、Dashboard 侧 SDL 与 Dashboard 生成的客户端产物三方不一致，App 扩展（含 NEW_TAB / WIDGET 目标与各页面挂载点）在两端契约上断裂。
2. **版本与构建声明未到达目标版本**。core 的 `pyproject.toml`、`package.json`、`saleor/__init__.py` 的 `__version__` 仍为 3.22.0；dashboard 的 `package.json` `version` 为 3.22.9、`saleor_schemaVersion` 为 "3.22"。
3. **依赖与构建声明差异**。`/opt/environment/dependencies/target/` 下提供了两仓库的目标依赖清单（saleor：`pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock`；saleor-dashboard：`package.json` + `pnpm-lock.yaml` + `pnpm-workspace.yaml`），其中包含新增依赖与脚本（如 dashboard 的 `generate:main` / `generate:staging` 及对应的 codegen 配置），需要在不破坏现有功能的前提下对齐。
4. **数据库迁移需保持一致且可部署**。基线已含 3.22 patch 迁移（如 `saleor/app/migrations/0031_alter_appextension_mount_alter_appextension_target.py`、`0032_appextension_http_target_method_and_more.py`，以及 site、order、payment 相关 patch 迁移），迁移链必须保持完整、可执行，且不产生未声明的模型漂移。

业务目标：

- G1：两仓库以普通源码改动方式完成到 3.23.0 的协同生产代码迁移，版本标识、GraphQL 契约、生成产物、数据库迁移与构建/依赖声明全部一致。
- G2：既有被回归测试覆盖的行为不被破坏；目标行为以真实生产代码实现，不得用测试专用桩替代缺失功能。
- G3：全程离线工作，不联网获取目标源码或安装包；改动以可导出 diff 的形式留在工作树中，供评测方对照固定基线评测。

验收总规则（引自 Instruction）："Evaluation runs the official tests before and after your changes. The intended acceptance rule requires all selected fail-to-pass tests to pass after your changes and all selected pass-to-pass tests to remain passing. Collection failures and missing selected results are not passes."

## 2. 用户与场景

- **商家管理员 / 运营人员**：通过 Dashboard 管理店铺。他们使用 App 扩展功能（页面内挂载的 WIDGET 小部件、NEW_TAB 新标签页跳转），依赖 Dashboard 与后端契约一致才能正常加载已安装 App 提供的扩展；同时也依赖订单/草稿订单筛选（`OrderWhereInput` / `DraftOrderWhereInput` 与搜索）、退款设置（`RefundSettings`）等既有功能在迁移后保持原行为。
- **App 作者 / API 消费者**：通过 GraphQL API 集成 Saleor。他们读取 `appExtensions` 查询结果来渲染自己的扩展入口，迁移后应能在同一份契约下取到 `mountName` / `targetName` / `settings`，且旧的 `mount` / `target` / `options` 字段在弃用期内继续可用。
- **平台运维 / 部署人员**：负责执行数据库迁移与部署。他们要求迁移链完整可执行、`makemigrations` 无漂移，依赖声明与锁文件一致且可离线安装。
- **平台研发与评测流程**：以四套本地回归套件（`core-unit`、`core-e2e`、`dash-unit`、`dash-e2e`，经 `/opt/runtime/run-suite.sh` 运行）和官方评测（fail-to-pass / pass-to-pass）判定迁移质量。

## 3. 需求条目

#### A. 版本与发布一致性

### R01 · 两仓库版本标识升级至 3.23.0
- 来源：Instruction 原文："The baselines are core 3.22.0 and dashboard 3.22.9; the intended target is 3.23.0." 及 "Keep the backend API and Dashboard behavior consistent, including their GraphQL contracts, generated client artifacts, database migrations, and build/dependency declarations."（版本号属于构建/依赖声明的一部分）。
- 优先级：P0
- 需求描述：将 core 仓库的版本声明从 3.22.0 升级为 3.23.0，涉及 `pyproject.toml` 的 `version`、根 `package.json` 的 `version`、`saleor/__init__.py` 的 `__version__`；将 dashboard 仓库 `package.json` 的 `version` 从 3.22.9 升级为 3.23.0，并将 `saleor_schemaVersion` 从 "3.22" 升级为 "3.23"。版本声明在各自仓库内不得出现互相矛盾（例如 `__version__` 与 `pyproject.toml` 不一致）。Dashboard 展示版本处的取值链（如 `src/config.ts` 中 `APP_VERSION` 基于 package.json version）应自然反映新版本，无需为此引入特殊逻辑。
- 验收条件：
  - AC-01-1：在 core 仓库中执行 `python -c "import saleor; print(saleor.__version__)"` 输出 `3.23.0`，且 `pyproject.toml` 与根 `package.json` 中的 `version` 均为 `3.23.0`。
  - AC-01-2：dashboard 仓库 `package.json` 中 `version` 为 `3.23.0` 且 `saleor_schemaVersion` 为 `"3.23"`。

#### B. GraphQL 契约与生成产物

### R02 · 后端 AppExtension API 补齐 3.22 patch 新字段并弃用旧字段
- 来源：Instruction 原文："Implement the coordinated production-code migration to 3.23.0 across both repositories. Keep the backend API and Dashboard behavior consistent, including their GraphQL contracts..."。推导依据：dashboard `schema.graphql` 已定义 `mountName: String!`、`targetName: String!`、`settings: JSON!` 并在 `mount`/`target`/`options` 上标注 `@deprecated(reason: "Use `mountName` instead.")` 等；dashboard `CHANGELOG.md` 3.22.9 说明已切换到新字段；而后端 `saleor/graphql/schema.graphql` 的 `type AppExtension` 与 `saleor/graphql/app/types.py` 的 `AppExtension` 类型尚无这三个字段——该差异为本迁移必须补齐的生产行为。
- 优先级：P0
- 需求描述：在后端 GraphQL 的 `AppExtension` 类型上新增 `mountName: String!`、`targetName: String!`、`settings: JSON!` 三个字段，以真实生产代码（resolver/类型定义）实现，语义与 Dashboard 现有消费方式一致：`mountName` 为扩展挂载点名称字符串（对应现有 `mount` 的取值），`targetName` 为目标名称字符串（对应现有 `target` 的取值），`settings` 为 JSON 对象，承载原 `options` 所表达的目标配置（包括 NEW_TAB 与 WIDGET 目标的 `method`，其来源为 `AppExtension` 模型的 `http_target_method` 字段）。同时将 `mount`、`target`、`options` 标记为弃用（deprecation 说明指向对应新字段），但三者继续按 3.22 现有行为返回数据，不得移除或改变其现有取值。`settings` 的 JSON 结构需与 Dashboard 侧解析器（`useExtensions.ts` / `AppWidgets.tsx` 中经 `appExtensionManifestOptionsSchema` 校验 `newTabTarget` / `widgetTarget`）兼容。实现不得依赖仅服务于测试的桩代码。
- 验收条件：
  - AC-02-1：后端 `saleor/graphql/schema.graphql` 中 `type AppExtension` 包含 `mountName: String!`、`targetName: String!`、`settings: JSON!`，且 `mount`、`target`、`options` 三者均带指向新字段的 `@deprecated` 指令。
  - AC-02-2：给定一个已安装且配置了扩展的 App（前置：通过现有 app 安装/扩展创建流程建立数据），执行 `appExtensions` 查询时返回的每条扩展记录中 `mountName` 与其 `mount` 取值对应、`targetName` 与其 `target` 取值对应、`settings` 为包含目标配置的 JSON 对象（NEW_TAB / WIDGET 场景下含目标 `method`，取自 `http_target_method`）。
  - AC-02-3：同一查询中 `mount`、`target`、`options` 字段仍返回与迁移前一致的值（弃用不改变行为）；对 `AppExtension` 模型已有数据执行查询不报错。

### R03 · GraphQL 契约与 Dashboard 生成产物对齐
- 来源：Instruction 原文："Keep the backend API and Dashboard behavior consistent, including their GraphQL contracts, generated client artifacts..."。
- 优先级：P0
- 需求描述：R02 完成后，Dashboard 仓库的 `schema.graphql` 与 core 仓库的 `saleor/graphql/schema.graphql` 在 AppExtension 相关契约（`type AppExtension`、相关 enum、`scalar JSON`）上保持一致，消除当前两份 SDL 之间的字段级差异。Dashboard 依据 schema 由 graphql-codegen 生成的客户端产物（`src/graphql/types.generated.ts`、`src/graphql/hooks.generated.ts`、`src/graphql/typePolicies.generated.ts`、`src/graphql/fragmentTypes.generated.ts`）须与最终 schema 同步再生成并提交，保证现有查询（如 `src/extensions/queries.ts` 的 `extensionList` 对 `mountName`/`targetName`/`settings` 的选择）在生成类型中可解析。生成过程须可离线完成（依赖已预装）。
- 验收条件：
  - AC-03-1：对两份 `schema.graphql` 做 diff，`AppExtension` 类型定义、其字段与弃用标注、以及 `AppExtension` 相关 enum 与 `scalar JSON` 声明不再存在字段级差异（允许与契约无关的差异，如文件内声明位置）。
  - AC-03-2：dashboard 中以仓库内 codegen 配置重新执行 graphql-codegen，生成的 `src/graphql/*.generated.ts` 与工作树中已提交内容一致（无未提交 diff），且 `AppExtension` 相关生成类型包含 `mountName`、`targetName`、`settings`。

#### C. 数据迁移与构建/依赖声明

### R04 · 数据库迁移一致性
- 来源：Instruction 原文："Keep the backend API and Dashboard behavior consistent, including ... database migrations, and build/dependency declarations." 及 "Preserve existing behavior covered by regression tests while implementing the target behavior."
- 优先级：P0
- 需求描述：保持 core 仓库现有迁移链完整且可执行，包括基线已有的 3.22 patch 迁移（如 `saleor/app/migrations/0031_alter_appextension_mount_alter_appextension_target.py`、`0032_appextension_http_target_method_and_more.py`，以及 site、order、payment 等 app 的对应 patch 迁移）。若本次改动产生新的模型状态变化，必须以正常新增迁移（`makemigrations` 产物）表达，不得手改既有迁移历史，也不得让模型与迁移出现未声明漂移。迁移需能在评测运行时的数据库上顺序执行成功。
- 验收条件：
  - AC-04-1：在 core 仓库执行 `python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run` 退出码为 0（无未生成的模型变更）。
  - AC-04-2：在评测运行时提供的数据库上执行 `python manage.py migrate` 成功完成，基线既有迁移（含 app/0031、app/0032 等）全部可应用，无报错。

### R05 · 依赖与构建/脚本声明对齐目标清单
- 来源：Instruction 原文："Keep the backend API and Dashboard behavior consistent, including ... build/dependency declarations." 及 "Required dependencies and development tools are preinstalled. Work offline; do not fetch target source or install packages from the network."。推导依据：`/opt/environment/dependencies/target/` 提供两仓库的目标依赖清单（saleor 的 `pyproject.toml`/`uv.lock`；saleor-dashboard 的 `package.json`/`pnpm-lock.yaml`/`pnpm-workspace.yaml`），需按既定策略对齐：目标清单声明的版本与新增依赖落入仓库声明，仅存在于基线而目标清单未包含的包（base-only，如 saleor 侧 Adyen、posuto，dashboard 侧 `@material-ui/icons`、`@saleor/sdk`）保留，不因对齐而移除其声明与功能代码。
- 优先级：P0
- 需求描述：将 core 的 `pyproject.toml` 依赖声明与 `uv.lock` 按 target 清单对齐（含目标新增依赖，如 `kombu[sqs]`、`nh3`、`idna`、`orjson` 等），保留 base-only 依赖；将 dashboard 的 `package.json` 与 `pnpm-lock.yaml` 按 target 清单对齐（含目标新增依赖，如 `@react-editor-js/core`、`history`、`moment`、`react-transition-group`、`sonner` 等），保留 base-only 依赖。对齐 dashboard 的构建/脚本声明：target 清单中的脚本差异（如 `generate:main` / `generate:staging` 指向的 `codegen-main.ts` / `codegen-staging.ts` 配置文件、`test` 聚合 `test:lint-rules` 等）应落到仓库中，缺失的配置文件一并补齐。所有依赖解析与安装校验均须离线完成，不得联网。
- 验收条件：
  - AC-05-1：core 仓库 `pyproject.toml` 的依赖声明包含 target 清单相对当前基线新增的依赖及其版本约束，`uv.lock` 与之一致可解析；base-only 依赖（如 Adyen、posuto）仍被声明，对应既有功能代码未被删除。
  - AC-05-2：dashboard 仓库 `package.json` 的依赖包含 target 清单新增依赖，`pnpm-lock.yaml` 与之一致；base-only 依赖（如 `@material-ui/icons`、`@saleor/sdk`）仍被声明；target 清单中的脚本差异已落到 `package.json`，引用的 codegen 配置文件存在于仓库中。
  - AC-05-3：离线校验通过：在预装依赖缓存下以离线方式完成安装/锁文件校验（如 dashboard `pnpm install --offline`、core `uv sync --offline` 或等效命令）全程无网络访问且成功结束。

#### D. 行为保持与交付约束

### R06 · 既有回归行为保持，目标行为以生产代码实现
- 来源：Instruction 原文："Preserve existing behavior covered by regression tests while implementing the target behavior. Do not replace missing production features with test-specific stubs." 及 "The intended acceptance rule requires all selected fail-to-pass tests to pass after your changes and all selected pass-to-pass tests to remain passing. Collection failures and missing selected results are not passes."
- 优先级：P0
- 需求描述：迁移过程中，所有被现有回归测试覆盖的行为保持不变，包括：core 的单元与 e2e 覆盖面（订单/草稿订单 where 与搜索过滤、`RefundSettings` 与 `reasonReference`、TransactionItem 支付方式详情（`PaymentMethodDetails`、`cc_*` 字段与 `update_payment_method_details`）、`Money.fractionalAmount`/`fractionDigits`、同步 webhook JSON schema（`saleor/json_schemas/` 及 `generate_json_schemas.py`）、App 扩展 NEW_TAB / WIDGET 行为等）与 dashboard 的 jest 单测、playwright e2e（含各页面挂载点 `extensionMountPoints.ts`、`ALL_APP_EXTENSION_MOUNTS`、`WIDGET_AVAILABLE_MOUNTS` 的现有语义）。目标行为（如 R02 新字段）必须以真实生产代码实现，禁止为通过测试而添加仅测试可用的桩、开关或特判。本地四套套件（`core-unit`、`core-e2e`、`dash-unit`、`dash-e2e`）不得因本次改动出现新增失败；官方评测的 fail-to-pass / pass-to-pass 规则以 Instruction 为准。
- 验收条件：
  - AC-06-1：使用 `/opt/runtime/run-suite.sh` 运行 `core-unit` 与 `dash-unit`，与基线相比不出现新增失败用例（改动前失败且未被本次要求修复的用例除外，需逐例可解释）。
  - AC-06-2：使用 `/opt/runtime/run-suite.sh` 运行 `core-e2e` 与 `dash-e2e`，与基线相比不出现新增失败场景。
  - AC-06-3：对最终 diff 审查确认：不存在仅服务于评测测试、无生产调用方的桩实现或特判逻辑；R02 的新字段由真实 resolver/类型定义支撑。
  - AC-06-4：官方评测语义下，选定的 fail-to-pass 测试在改动后全部通过，选定的 pass-to-pass 测试全部保持通过，无收集失败、无缺失结果。

## 4. 范围与非目标

本次包含：

- core 与 dashboard 两仓库内、为达成 R01–R06 所需的全部生产代码改动：GraphQL 类型与 resolver、`schema.graphql` 再生成、dashboard 生成产物再生成、数据库新增迁移、版本号与 `saleor_schemaVersion`、依赖声明与锁文件、构建脚本与 codegen 配置。
- 为使契约一致所需的代码内弃用标注（deprecation）与描述文案（含 `ADDED_IN_*` 版本标注的沿用风格）。

明确不做（非目标）：

- 不修改评测测试、fixtures、verifier 或评分配置；官方测试由评测方另行提供。
- 不从网络获取目标源码、不联网安装任何包；全部工作离线完成。
- 不删除或削弱 base-only 依赖对应的既有功能（如 Adyen 支付相关代码、`@saleor/sdk` 的使用），依赖对齐策略为"目标清单升级 + base-only 保留"。
- 不追求与 upstream 3.23.0 上游树逐字节一致；Instruction 明确测试代码可含 maintainer 提供的兼容 helper，评测树不要求逐字节等同。
- 不新增与迁移目标无关的新业务功能，不做顺带重构。
- 正式评分冻结（"maintainer acceptance and scoring-list freeze are pending"）属评测方事项，不在本迁移范围内。

## 5. 其他

- 事实依据：dashboard 3.22.9 的 `schema.graphql`、`src/extensions/queries.ts`、`useExtensions.ts`、`AppWidgets.tsx` 已消费 `mountName`/`targetName`/`settings`，且其 `CHANGELOG.md` 明确记载切换原因；core 基线已含多数 3.23 时代特性（`RefundSettings`、NEW_TAB/WIDGET、`PaymentMethodDetails`、`fractionalAmount`、`OrderWhereInput` 等），故 R02 是契约一致性的主要缺口，而非全面补功能。
- 版本取值事实：core 目标版本号以 `/opt/environment/dependencies/target/saleor/pyproject.toml` 的 `version = "3.23.0"` 为准；dashboard 以 `/opt/environment/dependencies/target/saleor-dashboard/package.json` 的 `version = "3.23.0"`、`saleor_schemaVersion = "3.23"` 为准。
- 依赖对齐策略依据：环境提供的 target 清单即"目标锁定版本"的权威来源；base-only 保留原则来自环境对依赖清单的说明（"base dependencies upgraded by target lockfiles; base-only packages retained"）。
- 假设：评测运行时会提供本地数据库与所需服务（`/opt/runtime/run-suite.sh` 已内置启停与健康检查）；官方测试可能包含 maintainer 兼容 helper，本迁移的实现不得依赖这些 helper 才能工作。
- 待确认项：无阻塞项。评测的 F2P/P2P 名单尚在维护方冻结流程中（Instruction 已声明），本 PRD 的验收条件以 Instruction 记载的总规则为准，不预设具体用例名单。

版本：v1

## 1. 业务背景与目标

Saleor 是面向商家的开源电商平台，本次工作范围覆盖两个仓库：`saleor/`（核心后端，Django + Graphene GraphQL）与 `saleor-dashboard/`（商家管理前端，React + TypeScript + Apollo Client）。当前基线为 core 3.22.0（agent-baseline 提交 c864e66 加环境补丁）与 dashboard 3.22.9（提交 aebb240 加环境补丁），目标版本为 3.23.0。

Instruction 明确要求："Implement the coordinated production-code migration to 3.23.0 across both repositories. Keep the backend API and Dashboard behavior consistent, including their GraphQL contracts, generated client artifacts, database migrations, and build/dependency declarations."

对现有代码的核查显示，本次协同迁移的核心缺口是：

1. **AppExtension GraphQL 契约不一致**。Dashboard 3.22.9 已经切换到 3.22 patch 引入的新字段（dashboard `CHANGELOG.md` 3.22.9 条目："Switched to the new AppExtension fields introduced in 3.22 patch (mount -> mountName, target -> targetName, options -> settings)"），`schema.graphql` 与 `src/extensions/queries.ts`、`src/extensions/hooks/useExtensions.ts`、`src/extensions/components/AppWidgets/AppWidgets.tsx` 均已消费 `mountName: String!`、`targetName: String!`、`settings: JSON!`，并对 `mount`/`target`/`options` 标注了 `@deprecated`。但后端 `saleor/graphql/schema.graphql` 与 `saleor/graphql/app/types.py` 尚未提供这三个字段，导致后端 SDL、Dashboard 侧 SDL 与 Dashboard 生成的客户端产物三方不一致，App 扩展（含 NEW_TAB / WIDGET 目标与各页面挂载点）在两端契约上断裂。
2. **版本与构建声明未到达目标版本**。core 的 `pyproject.toml`、`package.json`、`saleor/__init__.py` 的 `__version__` 仍为 3.22.0；dashboard 的 `package.json` `version` 为 3.22.9、`saleor_schemaVersion` 为 "3.22"。
3. **依赖与构建声明差异**。`/opt/environment/dependencies/target/` 下提供了两仓库的目标依赖清单（saleor：`pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock`；saleor-dashboard：`package.json` + `pnpm-lock.yaml` + `pnpm-workspace.yaml`），其中包含新增依赖与脚本（如 dashboard 的 `generate:main` / `generate:staging` 及对应的 codegen 配置），需要在不破坏现有功能的前提下对齐。
4. **数据库迁移需保持一致且可部署**。基线已含 3.22 patch 迁移（如 `saleor/app/migrations/0031_alter_appextension_mount_alter_appextension_target.py`、`0032_appextension_http_target_method_and_more.py`，以及 site、order、payment 相关 patch 迁移），迁移链必须保持完整、可执行，且不产生未声明的模型漂移。

业务目标：

- G1：两仓库以普通源码改动方式完成到 3.23.0 的协同生产代码迁移，版本标识、GraphQL 契约、生成产物、数据库迁移与构建/依赖声明全部一致。
- G2：既有被回归测试覆盖的行为不被破坏；目标行为以真实生产代码实现，不得用测试专用桩替代缺失功能。
- G3：全程离线工作，不联网获取目标源码或安装包；改动以可导出 diff 的形式留在工作树中，供评测方对照固定基线评测。

验收总规则（引自 Instruction）："Evaluation runs the official tests before and after your changes. The intended acceptance rule requires all selected fail-to-pass tests to pass after your changes and all selected pass-to-pass tests to remain passing. Collection failures and missing selected results are not passes."

## 2. 用户与场景

- **商家管理员 / 运营人员**：通过 Dashboard 管理店铺。他们使用 App 扩展功能（页面内挂载的 WIDGET 小部件、NEW_TAB 新标签页跳转），依赖 Dashboard 与后端契约一致才能正常加载已安装 App 提供的扩展；同时也依赖订单/草稿订单筛选（`OrderWhereInput` / `DraftOrderWhereInput` 与搜索）、退款设置（`RefundSettings`）等既有功能在迁移后保持原行为。
- **App 作者 / API 消费者**：通过 GraphQL API 集成 Saleor。他们读取 `appExtensions` 查询结果来渲染自己的扩展入口，迁移后应能在同一份契约下取到 `mountName` / `targetName` / `settings`，且旧的 `mount` / `target` / `options` 字段在弃用期内继续可用。
- **平台运维 / 部署人员**：负责执行数据库迁移与部署。他们要求迁移链完整可执行、`makemigrations` 无漂移，依赖声明与锁文件一致且可离线安装。
- **平台研发与评测流程**：以四套本地回归套件（`core-unit`、`core-e2e`、`dash-unit`、`dash-e2e`，经 `/opt/runtime/run-suite.sh` 运行）和官方评测（fail-to-pass / pass-to-pass）判定迁移质量。

## 3. 需求条目

#### A. 版本与发布一致性

### R01 · 两仓库版本标识升级至 3.23.0

- 优先级：P0
- 需求描述：将 core 仓库的版本声明从 3.22.0 升级为 3.23.0，涉及 `pyproject.toml` 的 `version`、根 `package.json` 的 `version`、`saleor/__init__.py` 的 `__version__`；将 dashboard 仓库 `package.json` 的 `version` 从 3.22.9 升级为 3.23.0，并将 `saleor_schemaVersion` 从 "3.22" 升级为 "3.23"。版本声明在各自仓库内不得出现互相矛盾（例如 `__version__` 与 `pyproject.toml` 不一致）。Dashboard 展示版本处的取值链（如 `src/config.ts` 中 `APP_VERSION` 基于 package.json version）应自然反映新版本，无需为此引入特殊逻辑。
- 验收条件：

  - AC-01-2：dashboard 仓库 `package.json` 中 `version` 为 `3.23.0` 且 `saleor_schemaVersion` 为 `"3.23"`。

#### B. GraphQL 契约与生成产物

### R02 · 后端 AppExtension API 补齐 3.22 patch 新字段并弃用旧字段
- 来源：Instruction 原文："Implement the coordinated production-code migration to 3.23.0 across both repositories. Keep the backend API and Dashboard behavior consistent, including their GraphQL contracts..."。推导依据：dashboard `schema.graphql` 已定义 `mountName: String!`、`targetName: String!`、`settings: JSON!` 并在 `mount`/`target`/`options` 上标注 `@deprecated(reason: "Use `mountName` instead.")` 等；dashboard `CHANGELOG.md` 3.22.9 说明已切换到新字段；而后端 `saleor/graphql/schema.graphql` 的 `type AppExtension` 与 `saleor/graphql/app/types.py` 的 `AppExtension` 类型尚无这三个字段——该差异为本迁移必须补齐的生产行为。
- 优先级：P0
- 需求描述：在后端 GraphQL 的 `AppExtension` 类型上新增 `mountName: String!`、`targetName: String!`、`settings: JSON!` 三个字段，以真实生产代码（resolver/类型定义）实现，语义与 Dashboard 现有消费方式一致：`mountName` 为扩展挂载点名称字符串（对应现有 `mount` 的取值），`targetName` 为目标名称字符串（对应现有 `target` 的取值），`settings` 为 JSON 对象，承载原 `options` 所表达的目标配置（包括 NEW_TAB 与 WIDGET 目标的 `method`，其来源为 `AppExtension` 模型的 `http_target_method` 字段）。同时将 `mount`、`target`、`options` 标记为弃用（deprecation 说明指向对应新字段），但三者继续按 3.22 现有行为返回数据，不得移除或改变其现有取值。`settings` 的 JSON 结构需与 Dashboard 侧解析器（`useExtensions.ts` / `AppWidgets.tsx` 中经 `appExtensionManifestOptionsSchema` 校验 `newTabTarget` / `widgetTarget`）兼容。实现不得依赖仅服务于测试的桩代码。
- 验收条件：
  - AC-02-1：后端 `saleor/graphql/schema.graphql` 中 `type AppExtension` 包含 `mountName: String!`、`targetName: String!`、`settings: JSON!`，且 `mount`、`target`、`options` 三者均带指向新字段的 `@deprecated` 指令。
  - AC-02-2：给定一个已安装且配置了扩展的 App（前置：通过现有 app 安装/扩展创建流程建立数据），执行 `appExtensions` 查询时返回的每条扩展记录中 `mountName` 与其 `mount` 取值对应、`targetName` 与其 `target` 取值对应、`settings` 为包含目标配置的 JSON 对象（NEW_TAB / WIDGET 场景下含目标 `method`，取自 `http_target_method`）。
  - AC-02-3：同一查询中 `mount`、`target`、`options` 字段仍返回与迁移前一致的值（弃用不改变行为）；对 `AppExtension` 模型已有数据执行查询不报错。

# Saleor Dashboard

## Project Overview

Saleor Dashboard is a GraphQL-powered, single-page React application built with TypeScript that serves as the admin interface for the Saleor e-commerce platform. It uses modern web technologies including React 17, @saleor/macaw-ui-next, Apollo Client, and Vite for bundling.

## Development Commands

### Basic Development

- `npm run dev` - Start development server on port 9000 with host binding, ALWAYS run this process in background, if you can't do that ask user
- `npm run build` - Build production bundle
- `npm run preview` - Preview production build locally

### Code Quality & Testing

Before completing changes make sure you run these commands:

- `npm run lint` - Run ESLint with auto-fix on src/ and playwright/ directories
- `npm run test:quiet <file_path>` - Run specific test file with console output suppressed
- `npm run check-types` - Run TypeScript type checking
- `npm run knip` - Check for unused files/dependencies/exports

#### Test Scripts

- `npm run test:quiet <file_path>` - RECOMMENDED: Run specific test with minimal output (--silent flag)
- `npm run test:debug <file_path>` - Run specific test file with full console output and extended React Testing Library output (DEBUG_PRINT_LIMIT=20000)

**Important for testing:**

- Always use `npm run test:quiet <file_path>` for specific files
- Use `npm run test:debug <file_path>` when you need to see full React component output for debugging
- Console output is suppressed in quiet command
- Tests automatically run from the `src/` directory (configured in jest.config.js)

### GraphQL & Code Generation

- `npm run generate` - Generate GraphQL types and hooks, after making changes in queries/mutations or updating schema
- `npm run fetch-schema` - Download GraphQL schema from Saleor repository
- `npm run fetch-local-schema` - Fetch schema from local Saleor instance

### Internationalization

- `npm run extract-messages` - Extract translatable messages from TypeScript files, run it after changing messages in `react-intl`

## Architecture Overview

### Module Structure

The codebase follows a feature-based architecture with shared components:

- **Feature Modules**: Each business domain (products, orders, customers, etc.) has its own directory containing:
  - `index.tsx` - Main feature export
  - `views/` - Page components and view logic
  - `components/` - Feature-specific components
  - `mutations.ts` - GraphQL mutations
  - `queries.ts` - GraphQL queries
  - `urls.ts` - Route definitions and URL helpers
  - `fixtures.ts` - Mock data for testing

- **Shared Components**: Reusable UI components in `/components/` directory organized by function
- **GraphQL Layer**: Generated types and hooks in `/graphql/` with fragment definitions in `/fragments/`
- **Services**: Business logic and utilities in `/services/` and `/utils/`

### Key Technologies

- **React 17** with TypeScript (strict mode disabled for old views using typescript-strict-plugin, new ones should use strict mode)
- **Apollo Client 3.4** for GraphQL state management
- **Vite** for build tooling and development server
- **React Hook Form** for form management
- **React Router v5** for navigation
- **React Intl** for internationalization
- **@saleor/macaw-ui-next** for UI components and design system

### TypeScript Configuration

- Base URL mapping with path aliases:
  - `@dashboard/*` → `src/*`
  - `@assets/*` → `assets/*`
  - `@locale/*` → `locale/*`
  - `@test/*` → `testUtils/*`
- Strict mode disabled but typescript-strict-plugin provides gradual strictness adoption
- ES2020 target with DOM libraries

### Build Configuration

- Vite with SWC for fast compilation and React refresh
- Source maps enabled for debugging
- Manual vendor chunk splitting for better caching
- Node polyfills for browser compatibility
- Sentry integration for error tracking in production

### Testing Setup

- Jest with SWC transformer for fast test execution
- Testing Library for React component testing
- Playwright for E2E testing
- Canvas mock and localStorage mock for browser APIs
- JSDOM test environment

## Development Workflow

### Before Starting Development

1. Ensure you have a running Saleor backend instance
2. Configure environment variables as described in `docs/configuration.md`
3. Run `npm run generate` to generate GraphQL types
4. Install dependencies with `npm i`

### Adding New Features

1. Create feature directory under appropriate domain (e.g., `/src/products/`)
2. Follow existing patterns for queries, mutations, and component structure
3. Use GraphQL fragments for consistent data fetching
4. Add proper TypeScript types and utilize path aliases
5. Include proper error handling and loading states

### Code Standards

- Use existing UI components from `/components/` directory
- Follow Material-UI theming patterns
- Utilize Apollo Client hooks for GraphQL operations
- Implement proper form validation with React Hook Form
- Add internationalization support for user-facing text

### Testing Requirements

- Write unit tests for utility functions and complex components
- Use Playwright for E2E testing of critical user flows
- Mock GraphQL operations in tests using fixtures
- Ensure type safety with TypeScript strict plugin

Add // Arrange // Act // Assert comments in tests to clarify test structure

## Git Conflict Resolution

### Auto-generated Files (DO NOT manually resolve)

These files should be regenerated after resolving source conflicts:

- `package-lock.json` - Run `npm install` after resolving `package.json`
- `src/graphql/hooks.generated.ts` - Run `npm run generate` after resolving GraphQL files
- `src/graphql/typePolicies.generated.ts` - Run `npm run generate` after resolving GraphQL files
- `src/graphql/fragmentTypes.generated.ts` - Run `npm run generate` after resolving GraphQL files
- `src/graphql/types.generated.ts` - Run `npm run generate` after resolving GraphQL files

### Package Version Conflicts

Always use the latest version when resolving package version conflicts between branches.

## Backend Integration

This frontend connects to a Saleor GraphQL backend:

- Default backend URL: http://localhost:8000/graphql/
- Configure via environment variables (see `docs/configuration.md`)
- Default development credentials for local Saleor instance: `admin@example.com` / `admin`
- Use `npm run fetch-local-schema` to sync GraphQL schema from local backend

## Package Updates

When modifying `package.json`, always run `npm install` to update `package-lock.json` and node_modules.

## Contributing

### Changesets

Use changesets CLI for user-facing changes that should appear in the changelog:

**Include in changesets:**

- Features: Provide detailed description with examples/screenshots
- Enhancements: Concise description of the improvement
- Bug fixes: Describe what didn't work → what works now

**Skip changesets for:**

- Internal refactors
- Code style changes
- Test additions
- CI/CD changes
- Documentation updates (unless user-facing)

### Pull Request Guidelines

PR descriptions should:

- Provide context for reviewers to understand the changes
- Explain non-obvious decisions or trade-offs
- Focus on the "why" rather than the "what" (code shows what)
- Include screenshots for UI changes
- Reference related issues or discussions

Once opening a pull request or working with GitHub directly, prefer to use `gh` cli to execute operations

## Code review

During code review, do not verify auto-generated files. Such files are suffixed with `.generated.ts`

def install_app(app_installation: AppInstallation, activate: bool = False):
    manifest_data = fetch_manifest(app_installation.manifest_url)
    assigned_permissions = app_installation.permissions.all()

    manifest_data["permissions"] = get_permission_names(assigned_permissions)

    clean_manifest_data(manifest_data, raise_for_saleor_version=True)

    app = App.objects.create(
        name=app_installation.app_name,
        is_active=activate,
        identifier=manifest_data.get("id"),
        about_app=manifest_data.get("about"),
        data_privacy=manifest_data.get("dataPrivacy"),
        data_privacy_url=manifest_data.get("dataPrivacyUrl"),
        homepage_url=manifest_data.get("homepageUrl"),
        support_url=manifest_data.get("supportUrl"),
        configuration_url=manifest_data.get("configurationUrl"),
        app_url=manifest_data.get("appUrl"),
        version=manifest_data.get("version"),
        manifest_url=app_installation.manifest_url,
        type=AppType.THIRDPARTY,
        audience=manifest_data.get("audience"),
        is_installed=False,
        author=manifest_data.get("author"),
    )

    app.permissions.set(app_installation.permissions.all())
    for extension_data in manifest_data.get("extensions", []):
        # Manifest is already "clean" so values are snake case
        options = extension_data.get("options", {})
        new_tab_target = options.get("new_tab_target")
        widget_target = options.get("widget_target")

        # Ensure proper extraction of the method values from the options
        http_target_method = None

        if (
            new_tab_target
            and isinstance(new_tab_target, dict)
            and "method" in new_tab_target
        ):
            http_target_method = new_tab_target["method"]

        if (
            widget_target
            and isinstance(widget_target, dict)
            and "method" in widget_target
        ):
            http_target_method = widget_target["method"]

        extension = AppExtension.objects.create(
            app=app,
            label=extension_data.get("label"),
            url=extension_data.get("url"),
            mount=extension_data.get("mount"),
            target=extension_data.get("target", AppExtensionTarget.POPUP),
            http_target_method=http_target_method,
        )
        extension.permissions.set(extension_data.get("permissions", []))

    webhooks = Webhook.objects.bulk_create(
        Webhook(
            app=app,
            name=webhook["name"],
            is_active=webhook["isActive"],
            target_url=webhook["targetUrl"],
            subscription_query=webhook["query"],
            custom_headers=webhook.get("customHeaders", None),
        )
        for webhook in manifest_data.get("webhooks", [])
    )

    webhook_events = []
    for db_webhook, manifest_webhook in zip(
        webhooks, manifest_data.get("webhooks", []), strict=False
    ):
        for event_type in manifest_webhook["events"]:
            webhook_events.append(
                WebhookEvent(webhook=db_webhook, event_type=event_type)
            )
    WebhookEvent.objects.bulk_create(webhook_events)

    _, token = app.tokens.create(name="Default token")  # type: ignore[call-arg] # calling create on a related manager # noqa: E501

I now have all the evidence I need. Let me now think about the design.

## Key facts established

**Backend (base 3.22.0, c864e66):**
- `saleor/graphql/app/types.py`:
  - `AppManifestExtension(BaseObjectType)` — fields permissions/label/url/mount/target; used for manifest-fetched extensions (dict roots from appFetchManifest / app install).
  - `AppExtension(AppManifestExtension, ModelObjectType[models.AppExtension])` — adds id/app/access_token/options.
  - `resolve_options` branches on target WIDGET/NEW_TAB returning options with method from `http_target_method`.
- `saleor/app/models.py` `AppExtension` model: app, label, url, mount (choices AppExtensionMount), target (choices, default POPUP), permissions M2M, `http_target_method` (nullable GET/POST).
- `saleor/app/types.py`: `AppExtensionMount` (str codes like `product_overview_more_actions`), `AppExtensionTarget` (popup/app_page/new_tab/widget), `AppExtensionHttpMethod` (GET/POST).
- `saleor/app/validators.py`: pydantic `NewTabTargetOptions`/`WidgetTargetOptions` (`method: Literal["GET","POST"]`), `AppExtensionOptions` (newTabTarget/widgetTarget aliases).
- `saleor/app/manifest_validations.py`: `_clean_extensions` normalizes manifest `target`/`mount` to snake-case enum values, validates widget mounts, `_clean_extension_options` stores `extension["options"] = validated_options.model_dump(exclude_none=True)` → keys `new_tab_target`/`widget_target` with `method`.
- `saleor/app/installation_utils.py install_app`: persists extension; extracts `http_target_method` from cleaned options; does NOT persist full options/settings (only method). So at query time, `settings` must be reconstructed the same way `options` is.
- `saleor/graphql/core/scalars.py`: `JSON` GenericScalar exists.
- `saleor/graphql/core/descriptions.py`: `ADDED_IN_322 = "\n\nAdded in Saleor 3.22."`.
- Deprecation idiom: `deprecation_reason="Use \`updatedAt\` instead."` on graphene fields.
- Schema regen: `pint build-schema` → `python manage.py get_graphql_schema > saleor/graphql/schema.graphql`.
- Version: `saleor/__init__.py __version__ = "3.22.0"`, `schema_version = f"{_major}.{_minor}"` → changing to 3.23.0 automatically changes schema_version to 3.23 and AppHeaders.SCHEMA_VERSION.
- Filters: `AppExtensionFilterInput { mount: [AppExtensionMountEnum!], target: AppExtensionTargetEnum }` — dashboard still filters by mount enum (useExtensions TODO comment says remove casting once API removes the enum). Keep unchanged.

**Dashboard (base 3.22.9, aebb240):**
- `schema.graphql` already has the target contract (mountName/targetName/settings on AppExtension AND AppManifestExtension; deprecations; scalar JSON moved).
- `src/extensions/queries.ts` `extensionList` query selects mountName/targetName/settings.
- `useExtensions.ts` consumes mountName/targetName/settings; filters query by `mount` enum.
- `AppWidgets.tsx` consumes targetName + settings (widgetTarget.method).
- `AppExtensionContextProvider` uses targetName POPUP etc.
- Generated artifacts: `src/graphql/types.generated.ts` etc. already contain mountName/targetName/settings — consistent with dashboard schema.graphql.
- `codegen.ts` exists; target package.json switches to codegen-main.ts/codegen-staging.ts + schema-main.graphql/schema-staging.graphql; these configs must be created.
- Target package.json: version 3.23.0, schemaVersion 3.23, new scripts (chromatic, dev:no-strict, e2e:clean-auth, fetch-schema:main/staging, generate:main/staging, graphql-lint-unused, test includes test:lint-rules, test-storybook, update-payment-assets), new deps (@react-editor-js/core, history, moment, react-transition-group, sonner), removed base-only deps (@material-ui/icons, @saleor/sdk).
- Target pnpm-lock.yaml is bigger (23738 lines vs 18473); node_modules already contains @react-editor-js and sonner — offline availability confirmed.
- lint/rules currently: named-styles.test.cjs exists, but target script references `lint/rules/named-styles.test.mjs` AND `lint/rules/named-effects.test.mjs` — named-effects doesn't exist yet; and .mjs vs .cjs naming. So the repair of scripts requires adding these files (or adjusting... no — target is authoritative; we need named-effects.test.mjs + rename to .mjs? Careful: target says `node lint/rules/named-styles.test.mjs && node lint/rules/named-effects.test.mjs`. We must create those files. This is part of R05/build alignment. As tech owner I design this.)
- `scripts/update-payment-assets.cjs` doesn't exist yet; target package.json references it → need to add the script file.
- Playwright: auth.setup.ts writes to `playwright/.auth`; target adds `e2e:clean-auth` script (rm -rf ./playwright/.auth) — trivial.

**Now, the central design question: what should the backend return for `mountName`, `targetName`, `settings`?**

From the dashboard SDL docs:
- `mountName: String!` — "Name of the extension mount point in the dashboard. Replaces `mount`" — i.e., the UPPER_SNAKE name (dashboard zod parses `ALL_APP_EXTENSION_MOUNTS` = "PRODUCT_OVERVIEW_MORE_ACTIONS" etc.).
- `targetName: String!` — "Name of the extension target in the dashboard. Replaces `target`" — UPPER values "NEW_TAB", "POPUP", "WIDGET", "APP_PAGE" (AppExtensionManifestTarget zod enum = ["POPUP","APP_PAGE","NEW_TAB","WIDGET"]).
- `settings: JSON!` — "App extension settings. Replaces `options` field." — dashboard zod `appExtensionManifestOptionsSchema` parses `{ newTabTarget: {method}, widgetTarget: {method} }` (camelCase keys!).

So:
- `mountName` = `root.mount.upper()` — actually convert mount code (`product_overview_more_actions`) to enum name (`PRODUCT_OVERVIEW_MORE_ACTIONS`).
- `targetName` = `root.target.upper()` (`popup` → `POPUP`).
- `settings` = `{"newTabTarget": {"method": ...}}` or `{"widgetTarget": {"method": ...}}` when target is NEW_TAB/WIDGET and http_target_method is set; otherwise `{}`.

The dashboard's `useExtensions` uses `settingsValidation.data?.newTabTarget?.method ?? "GET"` — fallback GET when validation fails or no data. And AppWidgets: `settingsValidation.success` must pass, else "Error rendering extension". For WIDGET extensions without settings... hmm: `appExtensionManifestOptionsSchema` is `z.object({newTabTarget optional, widgetTarget optional}).refine(not both)`. Empty object `{}` passes (both optional, refine passes). So `settings: {}` for POPUP/APP_PAGE is fine, and for WIDGET with method POST → `{"widgetTarget": {"method": "POST"}}`.

Wait — but for WIDGET target with `http_target_method=None`: settings would be `{}` → widget renders iframe as GET (isIframePost false → GET iframe). Good, consistent with options resolver which currently returns `AppExtensionOptionsWidget(widget_target=WidgetTargetOptions(method=None))` — hmm, actually current `resolve_options` passes `method=http_method` which may be None even though field is `required=True` in SDL. That's the existing behavior quirk. For settings, we should only include the target key when a method exists, or include it with method when set. Let me think about what upstream 3.23 does... I can't fetch it (offline, and instructed not to retrieve the upgraded schema — "仅采用给定 Base 与自行推导的设计"). So I derive: settings JSON mirrors the manifest `options` shape with camelCase keys, only containing target-specific settings when applicable.

Simplest consistent design derived from the dashboard consumers:
```python
def resolve_settings(root):
    http_method = root.http_target_method
    if root.target == WIDGET and http_method:
        return {"widgetTarget": {"method": http_method}}
    if root.target == NEW_TAB and http_method:
        return {"newTabTarget": {"method": http_method}}
    return {}
```
